title: OptAgent: Optimizing Query Rewriting for E-commerce via Multi-Agent Simulation

mechanism.domainTask: E-commerce query rewriting optimized with simulated-shopping relevance and purchase behavior
mechanism.populationDetail: A fixed-size pool of N query rewrites is evolved as generations; no island partition or maintained genealogy tree is described.
mechanism.archiveDetail: No separate archive is described; top alpha-N candidates survive inside each newly formed generation, and the best overall query is returned.
mechanism.replacementDetail: Each next generation retains the top M=alpha*N candidates from the current generation and fills remaining slots with offspring; this is generational replacement with elitist carryover.
mechanism.generationDetail: Initial rewrites are generated from the user's query; later offspring use true two-parent semantic crossover and one-parent small query mutations, sometimes applying mutation after crossover.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Five per-product semantic labels are averaged, then combined with top-10/all-product relevance and normalized purchase value into scalar F(q); the summarized-feedback generation step is not fully detailed.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: Top M = alpha × N candidates are admitted to the next-generation parent pool by fitness rank. For offspring generation Algorithm 1 calls SELECT(\(P_g\)) for one or two parents but does not specify the sampling distribution; count varies with crossover.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: A multi-agent simulated-shopping evaluator combines product retrieval, per-product semantic judgments, and agentic purchase decisions into query fitness; current evaluation fields capture its scalar and feedback properties but not the simulated-customer mechanism itself.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/OPTAGENT Optimizing Query Rewriting for ECommerce via Multi-Agent Simulation.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: The existing rank-based-selection citation is supported for the top-M survivor/parent-pool rule, but Algorithm 1 does not specify SELECT(P_g)'s mating-parent sampling distribution and uses one or two parents depending on crossover. Do not call the five temperature-varied evaluator instances a multi-model system or label the scalar fitness as pairwise preference evaluation.
